listening.title: Interview question: tell me about a failure

lines.speaker: Ms. Trang (HR Manager)
lines.text: Duc, can you tell me about a time when something went wrong at work?

lines.speaker: Duc (Candidate)
lines.text: Yes. Last year I led a small website project, and we delivered it two weeks late.

lines.speaker: Ms. Trang (HR Manager)
lines.text: Two weeks is quite a lot. What was the situation exactly?

lines.speaker: Duc (Candidate)
lines.text: We had three people and a very short timeline. I promised the client a date that was too early.

lines.speaker: Ms. Trang (HR Manager)
lines.text: So the plan was the problem, not the team?

lines.speaker: Duc (Candidate)
lines.text: That is right. I took on too much and did not check the workload carefully.

lines.speaker: Ms. Trang (HR Manager)
lines.text: How did you handle it when you saw the delay coming?

lines.speaker: Duc (Candidate)
lines.text: I told the client early, took the blame, and gave them a new plan with clear steps.

lines.speaker: Duc (Candidate)
lines.text: They were not happy, but they stayed with us because I was honest about the reason.

lines.speaker: Ms. Trang (HR Manager)
lines.text: And what did you learn from that experience?

lines.speaker: Duc (Candidate)
lines.text: After some self-reflection, I now give a realistic estimate and ask for help sooner. That was a valuable lesson.

questions.q: How late was the project delivered?
What does Duc say was the main cause?
options: He promised a date that was too early
One team member left the company

questions.q: What did the client decide to do?

shadowing: Last year I led a small project, and we delivered it two weeks late.
The main cause was simple: I took on too much at the same time.
I told the client early, took the blame, and offered a clear new plan.
Since then I always give a realistic estimate and ask for help sooner.
That failure was a valuable lesson, and it helped me improve my process.
